audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may bypass the owner-earnings capital-charge deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.2 million in 2025, $2.9 million in 2024, and $2.4 million in 2023; the 2025 amount equals 4.6% of the $69.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease principal appears in financing cash flow rather than capex, so an unadjusted CFO-minus-capex calculation adds back leased-asset amortization without charging the corresponding replacement outlay, overstating OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has operating leases for certain service centers, office space and equipment as well as finance leases, substantially all related to information technology equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The payments are demonstrated, but their omission from OE is only a possibility because the supplied calculation detail does not show whether they were separately deducted. Even treating the entire $3.2 million as a recurring reduction to the anchor would reduce bull value by approximately $1.85 per share to $39.31, still 22.8% below the $50.92 market price; it would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each annual OE reconciliation for a separate finance-lease-principal or leased-asset replacement charge; if absent, deduct the filed payments and refit the log-trend anchor.

audit_findings.title: Joint-and-several legacy pension exposure may exceed the recorded liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.0 million recorded MEPP liability at December 31, 2025; additional joint-and-several exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Payments not already embedded in normalized OE would reduce future equity cash flows, while an incremental liability attributable to pre-existing obligations could require a direct reduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: There can be no assurance that the Company’s actual future liabilities relating to the MEPP liabilities (including MEPP liabilities where the Company and RRD remain jointly and severally liable) will not differ materially from the amount recorded on the Company’s audited Consolidated Financial Statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The joint-and-several obligation and recorded $8.0 million liability are demonstrated, but no filed amount establishes DFIN's exposure beyond that liability. Because liability can shift to DFIN if RRD or other employers fail to pay, the downside could affect value, but the record cannot establish its magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain plan-by-plan gross withdrawal liabilities, payment schedules, DFIN and RRD allocation or indemnity agreements, RRD credit evidence, and the amount of recurring MEPP payments already included in OE; then deduct only the present value not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The latest debt burden may not match the historical interest-bearing numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Net debt increased $32.7 million from $171.3 million to $204.0 million; at the reported 6.0% revolver rate this represents approximately $2.0 million of annual pre-tax interest, while first-half 2026 net interest was $6.3 million versus $6.9 million in first-half 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, debt principal is not deducted, but interest on any sustained incremental borrowing must reduce projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had $110.7 million outstanding under its Term Loan A Facility, as defined below, and $61.0 million of borrowings outstanding under its Revolving Facility, as defined below.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher quarter-end debt is demonstrated, but a missing interest burden is not: first-half net interest actually declined, and the record does not establish that the June revolver balance is permanent. The issue becomes valuation-relevant prospectively only if the added borrowing persists or grows.
audit_findings.action: Compare average debt and interest incurred in the next filing with the June 30 balance; if the additional borrowing persists, replace historical interest in normalized OE with the current after-tax run rate and rerun the valuation without deducting principal.

audit_findings.title: A cash-tax timing benefit may have been treated as sustainable owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 cash taxes fell $16.2 million from $40.8 million to $24.6 million, primarily due to the Act; that reduction equals 18.3% of 2025 OE and 23.3% of the $69.5 million anchor before trend attenuation
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary reduction in cash taxes raises CFO and annual OE; including that observation without a normalized tax charge can raise the fitted log-trend anchor and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects certain provisions of the Act to change the timing of cash tax payments related to 2025 and future periods, but does not expect the enacted legislation to have a material impact on its income tax expense in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a substantial cash-tax timing benefit, although it does not demonstrate that the OE calculation failed to normalize it or that the full $16.2 million is temporary. Its scale relative to both latest OE and the anchor makes it reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor, intrinsic-value range, and buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 cash taxes to normalized accrual taxes excluding nonrecurring pension effects, quantify deductions accelerated by the Act and their reversal schedule, recompute 2025 OE, refit the ten-year log trend, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure $25.3 million, or $0.93 per diluted share; $3.3 million was domestic and $22.0 million international at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating cash or repatriation friction should reduce the $25.3 million cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents were $24.5 million at December 31, 2025, which included $3.5 million in the U.S. and $21.0 million at international locations.
audit_findings.explanation: The absence of a documented excess-cash analysis is demonstrated, but the nondistributable amount is unresolved. Even removing all cash—a conservative upper bound—would reduce bull value only to approximately $40.23 per share, still 21.0% below the $50.92 price, and reduce buy-below from $25.87 to approximately $25.22. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum seasonal operating cash and identify which foreign balances are previously taxed and freely transferable; adjust only the bridge for any unavailable amount.
